THE OKONKWO-BRIGHTWATER FAMILY IRREVOCABLE TRUST

TRUST AGREEMENT

This Trust Agreement is made on August 3, 2026, between Chinelo Okonkwo-Brightwater, of Evanston, Illinois (the "Settlor"), and Marisol Etxeberria and Whitcombe Trust Company, N.A. (together, the "Trustees").

ARTICLE ONE — CREATION AND IRREVOCABILITY

1.1 Transfer. The Settlor transfers to the Trustees the property listed on Schedule A, and any property later added by the Settlor or by any other person, to be held, administered, and distributed as provided in this Trust Agreement. The trust created by this instrument is named the Okonkwo-Brightwater Family Irrevocable Trust (the "Trust").

1.2 Irrevocability. This Trust is irrevocable. The Settlor reserves no power to alter, amend, revoke, or terminate this Trust, in whole or in part, and no power to change any beneficial interest under it. The Settlor may not be added as a beneficiary, and no trust property may be distributed to the Settlor or applied to discharge any legal obligation of the Settlor.

ARTICLE TWO — BENEFICIARIES AND DISTRIBUTIONS

2.1 Beneficiaries. The beneficiaries of this Trust are the Settlor's descendants, from time to time living.

2.2 Distribution Standard During the Settlor's Life. The Trustees may distribute so much of the net income and principal of the Trust as the Trustees determine necessary for the health, education, maintenance, and support of any beneficiary, an ascertainable standard within the meaning of Section 2041(b)(1)(A) of the Internal Revenue Code. In exercising this discretion the Trustees may, but need not, consider a beneficiary's other resources. No distribution may be made in the absolute discretion of a Trustee who is also a beneficiary; a distribution to a Trustee who is a beneficiary may be made only by an Independent Trustee and only under the ascertainable standard.

2.3 Distribution on the Settlor's Death. On the Settlor's death the Trustees shall divide the remaining trust property into equal shares, one share for each then-living child of the Settlor and one share for the then-living descendants, collectively, of each deceased child. Each share shall be held as a separate trust on the terms of Section 2.2 until the beneficiary reaches thirty-five (35), at which time the Trustees shall distribute the balance to the beneficiary outright.

ARTICLE THREE — WITHDRAWAL RIGHTS

3.1 Crummey Withdrawal Right. On each contribution to the Trust, each beneficiary then living has the right to withdraw an amount equal to the lesser of the contribution divided by the number of beneficiaries and the federal gift tax annual exclusion amount then in effect. The withdrawal right is a power of withdrawal exercisable by written notice to the Trustees.

3.2 Notice. The Trustees shall give each beneficiary, or the parent or guardian of a minor beneficiary, written notice of each contribution and of the right to withdraw within ten (10) days after the contribution. The withdrawal right lapses thirty (30) days after the notice is given.

3.3 Lapse Limit. A lapse of a withdrawal right in any calendar year is limited to the greater of $5,000 and 5% of the value of the trust property, and any portion of the right that would lapse in excess of that amount does not lapse but remains exercisable as a hanging power until it may lapse within the 5-or-5 limit in a later year.

ARTICLE FOUR — SPENDTHRIFT

4.1 Spendthrift Provision. No beneficial interest in this Trust, whether in income or principal, may be voluntarily transferred, assigned, pledged, or encumbered by a beneficiary, nor involuntarily transferred, reached, attached, garnished, or otherwise subjected to the claims of a beneficiary's creditors, and this provision is a spendthrift provision within the meaning of Section 502 of the Uniform Trust Code as enacted in the governing jurisdiction. A beneficiary's interest is not subject to the claims of any creditor and may not be reached by legal or equitable process before the Trustees actually distribute it.

ARTICLE FIVE — TRUSTEES

5.1 Powers. The Trustees shall have the power to retain, sell, exchange, lease, mortgage, and otherwise deal with any trust property; to invest and reinvest in any property, without regard to any rule limiting investment to legal investments; to allocate receipts and disbursements between income and principal; to borrow and lend; to vote securities and to participate in reorganizations; to hold property in the name of a nominee; to employ counsel, accountants, investment advisers, and agents and to pay their reasonable compensation; to make tax elections; to divide or consolidate trusts; and to do all other acts a prudent trustee would do, subject in every case to the Trustees' fiduciary duties.

5.2 Independent Trustee. "Independent Trustee" means a Trustee who is not the Settlor, is not a beneficiary, is not related or subordinate to the Settlor within the meaning of Section 672(c) of the Internal Revenue Code, and has no power to make a distribution to themselves.

5.3 Succession, Resignation, and Removal. A Trustee may resign on thirty (30) days written notice to the then-serving co-trustee and to the adult beneficiaries. If a Trustee resigns, dies, or becomes unable to serve, the remaining Trustee shall continue to serve and may appoint a successor trustee that is not related or subordinate to the Settlor. A majority of the adult beneficiaries may remove a corporate Trustee, with or without cause, on sixty (60) days written notice, provided a successor corporate trustee is appointed at the same time.

5.4 Trust Protector. The Settlor appoints Ezekiel Nwosu-Hart as Trust Protector. The Trust Protector may remove and replace a Trustee, may change the situs and governing law of the Trust, and may amend the administrative provisions of this Trust Agreement to conform to changes in law, but may not enlarge any beneficial interest, may not add a beneficiary, and may not exercise any power in the Trust Protector's own favor.

ARTICLE SIX — TAX PROVISIONS

6.1 Grantor Trust Status. The Settlor retains the power, exercisable in a nonfiduciary capacity, to reacquire trust property by substitution of property of equivalent value, so that the Trust is a grantor trust as to the Settlor under Section 675(4)(C) of the Internal Revenue Code. This power is exercisable without the approval or consent of any person in a fiduciary capacity.

6.2 Tax Reimbursement. An Independent Trustee may, in the Independent Trustee's sole discretion, reimburse the Settlor for, or pay the income tax attributable to, the Trust's income that is taxable to the Settlor. Neither the Settlor nor any beneficiary may compel a reimbursement, and no reimbursement may be made under a binding agreement or an established pattern.

ARTICLE SEVEN — ADMINISTRATION

7.1 Situs and Governing Law. The initial situs and principal place of administration of this Trust is Illinois, and the validity, construction, and administration of this Trust are governed by the laws of the State of Illinois.

7.2 Change of Situs and Decanting. The Trust Protector, or if none is serving an Independent Trustee, may change the situs and the principal place of administration of the Trust to another jurisdiction and may elect that the law of that jurisdiction governs the administration of the Trust. An Independent Trustee may decant by distributing all or part of the trust property to a second trust for the benefit of one or more of the beneficiaries, provided the second trust does not add a beneficiary and does not reduce any vested interest.

7.3 Accountings. The Trustees shall render an accounting to the adult beneficiaries at least annually.

The Settlor and the Trustees have signed this Trust Agreement on the date first written above.

Chinelo Okonkwo-Brightwater, Settlor
